title: South India Hill Stations Itinerary: Ooty, Kodaikanal and Munnar
seoTitle: South India Hill Stations Itinerary: 8 Days | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: A day-by-day South India hill stations itinerary: Ooty, Coonoor, Kodaikanal and Munnar in eight days, with the toy train, e-pass rules and seasons.
description: A practical eight-day South India hill stations itinerary: the Nilgiri Mountain Railway to Coonoor and Ooty, Kodaikanal in the Palani hills, and Munnar's tea estates, ending in Kochi, with approximate drive times, the Tamil Nadu e-pass, seasons, where to stay, and extensions to Thekkady, the backwaters, Coorg or Wayanad.
dek: Ooty, Kodaikanal and Munnar are the south's great hill-station trio. This route links them in about eight days.

hero.alt: Tea plantations at Coonoor in the Nilgiris

intro: The Nilgiris, the Palani hills and the Munnar hills are linked by winding but manageable roads, making a natural week-long loop. Start at Coimbatore, climb to the Nilgiris by toy train, cross to Kodaikanal, and finish in Munnar before descending to Kochi.
The route is best from October to May. Ooty and Kodaikanal require a free e-pass for vehicles registered outside those districts.
quickAnswer: An eight-day South India hill stations itinerary: Coimbatore to Mettupalayam and the Nilgiri toy train to Coonoor (day 1), Coonoor's tea estates (day 2), Ooty (days 3 to 4), drive to Kodaikanal (day 5), Kodaikanal (day 6), drive to Munnar (day 7) and Munnar's tea estates and Eravikulam before heading to Kochi (day 8). October to May is best; vehicles need an e-pass for Ooty and Kodaikanal.
takeaways: Start at Coimbatore and end at Kochi to avoid backtracking.
Take the Nilgiri toy train from Mettupalayam to Coonoor or Ooty; book early.
Ooty to Kodaikanal and Kodaikanal to Munnar are each a long day's drive.
Get e-passes for Ooty and Kodaikanal if your vehicle is registered outside those districts.
Extend with Thekkady and the backwaters, or with Coorg and Wayanad.

rows: Coimbatore to Mettupalayam; toy train to Coonoor
Tea estates, Sim's Park, Dolphin's Nose
Botanical Garden, Ooty Lake, rose garden
Doddabetta, Pykara, or the tea factory
Drive via Coimbatore and Palani (a long day)
Lake, Coaker's Walk, Pillar Rocks, forest trails
Drive via Bodinayakanur and Top Station
Tea museum, Eravikulam (when open), then down to Kochi

items.name: Coonoor and Ooty
body: Tea country and quieter stays at Coonoor; gardens, lakes and Doddabetta at Ooty.

image.caption: Nilgiri tea gardens

items.name: Kodaikanal
body: The lake, Coaker's Walk, Pillar Rocks, Bryant Park and forest trails.

items.name: Munnar
body: Tea estates, the tea museum, Mattupetty and Top Station, and Eravikulam National Park (closed for a period each year during the Nilgiri tahr calving season).

sections.heading: Extensions
list: Thekkady and Alappuzha: add three days for Periyar and a houseboat night on the backwaters.
Coorg and Mysuru: start in Bengaluru, visit Coorg, then enter the Nilgiris via Mudumalai (daylight only).
Valparai: a detour from Coimbatore or Pollachi for tea and wildlife.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: Coonoor and Kotagiri are quieter than Ooty town; heritage bungalows and estate stays are common. In Kodaikanal, stay near the lake or a little outside for views. In Munnar, resorts on the estate slopes have the best views, while stays in town are convenient but busier.

sections.heading: About the drives
paras: The ghat roads between these hill stations are long and winding. Ooty to Kodaikanal typically takes most of a day via Coimbatore and Palani, and Kodaikanal to Munnar about five to six hours via Bodinayakanur and the Bodimettu ghat. Start early, carry snacks and motion-sickness remedies, and avoid driving after dark on forest roads.

sections.heading: Food to try
list: Nilgiri tea and homemade chocolates in Ooty and Coonoor.
Varkey biscuits from the Nilgiri bakeries.
Kerala meals and appam with stew in Munnar.

sections.heading: When to go
list: October to February: cool and dry; the best time.
March to May: busy; book early.
June to September: heavy monsoon rain in the Nilgiris and Munnar.

safety: Drive times are approximate and depend on traffic, weather, landslides and road works; allow extra time and avoid driving after dark.
Vehicles registered outside the Nilgiris and Dindigul districts need a free e-pass for Ooty and Kodaikanal; check the Tamil Nadu e-pass portal.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
packing: Light warm layers; nights are cold in Ooty and Kodaikanal
Motion-sickness tablets for the ghat roads

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Ooty, Kodaikanal and Munnar?
faqs.a: About eight days by road; six is possible if you skip Coonoor.

faqs.q: What is the best order to visit?
faqs.a: Ooty, then Kodaikanal, then Munnar, starting at Coimbatore and ending at Kochi.
Vehicles registered outside the Nilgiris and Dindigul districts need free e-passes for Ooty and Kodaikanal.

faqs.q: Should I take the Nilgiri toy train?
faqs.a: Yes, at least the section from Mettupalayam to Coonoor; book early.

faqs.q: When is the best time for this trip?
faqs.a: October to May; the monsoon is very wet in the Nilgiris and Munnar.

faqs.q: Can I do this route by public transport?
faqs.a: Buses link all three hill stations, but a hired car saves time and allows viewpoint stops.
Yes; the three towns have gardens, lakes, boating and easy walks, but break up the long drives.
